title: Nut-Free Funfetti Cupcakes
shortDescription: Light buttery funfetti cupcakes with naturally colored sprinkles, ready in about 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These funfetti cupcakes use a light buttery vanilla base folded with naturally colored sprinkles, so you get all the confetti fun without any nuts in the batter or on top. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen with three different sprinkle brands to find ones that do not bleed color into the batter The crumb stays soft and fine because the butter and sugar get a long creaming time before the eggs go in. That extra air makes a real difference in the final texture. This is a solid party recipe for school bake sales or birthday tables where nut allergies matter. The frosting is a simple vanilla buttercream that lets the sprinkles inside the cake stay the star. You do not need any special equipment here, just a hand mixer and a muffin pan. It is an easy recipe even for a first time baker.
ingredients: 1/3 cup naturally colored sprinkles, plus 2 tbsp for topping
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl and set aside.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and granulated sugar on medium speed for 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract until smooth.
Add the flour mix in three batches, alternating with the milk, mixing just until combined.
Fold in 1/3 cup sprinkles by hand with a spatula to avoid streaking the batter.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat 1 cup butter for frosting until smooth, then add powdered sugar and cream, beating until fluffy.
Pipe frosting onto cooled cupcakes and finish with the remaining 2 tablespoons of sprinkles.
tips: Chop chunky sprinkles into smaller pieces so they do not sink to the bottom of the cupcake.
Check sprinkle labels for nut-free certification, since some factories process near tree nuts.
Fold sprinkles in gently and quickly. Overmixing turns the batter a muddy gray color.
Room temperature eggs and butter blend smoother and give a finer, more even crumb.

faq.question: Why did my sprinkles bleed color into the batter?
faq.answer: Some dyed sprinkles are not shell coated and will bleed when mixed too long. Use naturally colored sprinkles and fold them in fast, right before baking.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted in an airtight container at room temperature. Frost them the day you plan to serve.

faq.question: Are naturally colored sprinkles actually nut-free?
faq.answer: Most are, but always check the package for a nut-free label or allergy statement. Brands vary, so this is worth confirming each time you buy a new bag.

faq.question: Can I use this batter for a layer cake instead?
faq.answer: Yes, this recipe works in two 6 inch round pans. Bake at 350°F for about 25 minutes and check with a toothpick before pulling them out.

conclusion: These funfetti cupcakes give you the party look without any nut risk on the ingredient list. Keep the sprinkles natural and the mixing gentle, and you will get a soft, even crumb every time.
